algorithms.name: A check run that did not judge the work
steps: When a pre-review run ends, take what ended it.
Merge conflict: send the task back to its builder as merge-needed, naming the files. Start no new run until the branch changes.
The Hub stopped: at the next start, request a new run for every task still waiting for its pre-review result.

Error of any other kind, or a check that ran out of time with no failing test of the task's own named: if the previous run on the same task work was not itself such a retry, request one run on the current main tip.
Otherwise (the retry ended the same way): request nothing more, put the run and its error on the operator's Needs-you list, and leave the task's status unchanged.
Any other failure: the task's own failure, as today (sent back as broken-check or flaky).

design:
The phase is a per-check property the operator sets in the project's check settings: `review`, `landing` or `both`. A check saved before this change reads as `both`, so behaviour changes only for a project that opts in. A fast check gates an agent's completion, which happens before review, so it cannot be landing-only. Three values are enough for this slice (operator, 2026-11-04); running only when the machine is idle is slice 4.

Giving way means the operating system schedules every process a check starts, the check's whole process tree, below the user's interactive work. On a quiet machine the checks still get the whole processor, so nothing is slower unless the user is using the machine. It is a property of how the Hub starts the check, not of the check's command, so it works for any project's commands. It is a project setting, off by default (operator, 2026-11-04): no existing project's checks change speed without its say. The operator turns it on for this project.

What ended a run decides what happens next (see algorithms). The rule underneath: only a result that judged the work may count against the task. Everything else either goes to whoever can fix it (a conflict goes to the builder, operator 2026-11-04) or is retried a bounded number of times and then reaches the operator. The bound matters for other projects, whose checks may be long builds or paid CI time.

Supersedes: the vault fact fct-c1dfbea42f5e (from the CRFWM retrospective, src-518e204db0f2) records that, after CRFWM, an `error` or `interrupted` run on an older tip is retried only at the next refresh or approval. That is the behaviour this slice replaces, deliberately: FR-8 re-runs after a Hub stop at the next start, and FR-9 retries any other error once at once. The fact stays true of the system until this slice lands; once it does, the vault source is to be annotated as superseded by this document.

Acceptance drive (written before the build, failing on master): on a scratch Hub with a scratch git project whose checks are a quick 'lint' (review), a 'suite' (landing) whose command prints its own priority, and a 'slow' check that sleeps past its limit, complete a task and read GET /tasks/{id}/checks and the project settings route. On master the suite runs before review at normal priority and the slow check sends the task back; after the build the suite reads 'runs at landing', the slow check is retried once and lands on Needs-you, and with giving way on the suite reports below-normal priority at landing.

No process priority is set anywhere in the file.

open_questions.question: A merge conflict found before review: send the task back to its builder as merge-needed, or show it to the operator first? Answered (operator, 2026-11-04): back to the builder.
Should 'checks give way to the user' be on by default? Answered (operator, 2026-11-04): off by default for every project; the operator turns it on for this one.
Are three phases (review, landing, both) enough, or is a fourth such as 'only when idle' needed now? Answered (operator, 2026-11-04): three are enough; idle is slice 4.

problem:
Every configured check runs both before review and again in the landing batch. A project cannot keep a slow suite for landing only, so on this project hub-tests runs about 4.7 times per task (roadmap baseline, 1-3 Nov 2026). Check processes run at normal priority beside the user's own applications. On the night of 3-4 Nov two full suites ran side by side, both crashed their test workers after about 45 minutes, and each re-ran for another 32 (retrospectives of a-check-run-finishes-when-master-moves and the-build-dialog-redesigned, chk-b163130f844c and chk-e00281f3f705).

A run that ends without judging the work is handled badly:
- All 13 `error` runs on proj-d85a82bf4216 are merge conflicts ('X does not merge cleanly onto Y', hub/hub/project_checks.py:244). Before review nothing sends that task back: only landing does (landing_queue.py:1143, merge-needed), and approval is refused (requirement_gate.py:356) while the task sits.
- A run whose time limit ends it is recorded as failed (`failed()` treats `timed_out` as failure, project_checks.py:918-921). Unless the same check fails on master too, it is the task's own failure and sends the work back as broken-check, although running out of time on a busy machine says nothing about the work.
- After CRFWM, an `error` or `interrupted` run on an older master tip waits for the next refresh or an approval before it is run again (CRFWM retrospective, lesson 1; vault fact fct-c1dfbea42f5e). This slice changes that on purpose (FR-8, FR-9).
- A project chooses each check's time limit without seeing how long that check normally takes.

requirements.rationale: Opt-in: no project's gates change unless it chooses.
requirements.statement: Each check in a project's check settings carries a phase of review, landing or both. The operator can set it per check, and a check saved before this change reads and behaves as both.

A check whose phase is landing does not run in a task's pre-review check run. The task's checks show it as 'runs at landing', not as passed or skipped, and review and approval are not held waiting for it.
A check whose phase is review does not run in a landing batch's check run, and a landing batch is not held waiting for it.
Saving a check that is both fast and landing-only is refused with a message saying a fast check gates an agent's completion before review, so it cannot be landing-only.

While the project's 'checks give way to the user' setting is on, every process a check run starts, including the processes those start, runs at a scheduling priority below the priority of a normally started user application on the same machine.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-04: no project's checks change speed without its say.
requirements.statement: The 'checks give way to the user' setting is off for every project until the operator turns it on, including projects that existed before this change. While it is off, check processes run at the priority they run at today.

requirements.rationale: All 13 error runs on this project were conflicts; re-running one on the same tips repeats it. The builder can resolve it; the operator chose the builder over themselves (2026-11-04).
requirements.statement: When a pre-review check run cannot merge the task's work onto the main branch, the task is sent back to its builder with reason class merge-needed and notes naming the conflicting files. No further check run starts for that task until its branch has new commits.

requirements.rationale: Deliberately replaces today's behaviour, recorded in vault fact fct-c1dfbea42f5e (an interrupted run waits for the next refresh or approval): nothing about the work was judged, so the task should not wait on an unrelated event to be checked.
requirements.statement: A check run ended because the Hub stopped is requested again when the Hub next starts, for every task still waiting for its pre-review result, without waiting for a main-branch move or an approval.

requirements.rationale: Deliberately replaces today's behaviour, recorded in vault fact fct-c1dfbea42f5e (an errored run waits for the next refresh or approval). Bounded at one retry so a project whose checks are long builds or paid time is not charged for a loop.
requirements.statement: A check run that ends in error for any reason other than a merge conflict is requested once more automatically on the current main tip. A second consecutive error on the same task work is not retried: it appears in the operator's Needs-you list with the error text and the task, and the task is not sent back to its builder.

requirements.rationale: Running out of time on a busy machine says nothing about the work; a named failing test does.
requirements.statement: A check that runs past its time limit, and whose output names no failing test as the task's own, does not count as the task's failure: it is retried and surfaced like a Hub fault (hub-fault-retried-once). A check whose output names failing tests that are not failing on main still counts as the task's failure, as today.
Beside each check's time limit, the check settings show how long that check usually takes: the median and the longest of its last 20 passing results in this project, or 'no passing runs yet'.

in_scope: A per-check phase setting (review, landing, both) in the project's check settings, and the check runs and gates obeying it
A project setting, off by default, under which check processes and everything they start run below normal scheduling priority
Routing of check runs that did not judge the work: merge conflict, Hub stopped, Hub fault, check out of time
Each check's usual duration shown beside its time limit in the check settings
non_goals: Changing the Hub's limit of two concurrent check runs (roadmap non-goal); one full suite at a time for this repository is slice 3, project-only
Changing what the landing check requires: every check whose phase includes landing runs on the exact merged tree, as today
Running checks in the project's CI: that belongs to the pull-request landing roadmap (work-lands-through-pull-requests), not this one
Choosing check time limits automatically; the project still sets them
Changing this repository's own check configuration (for example lowering hub-tests' 3600s limit, or turning giving way on): that is the operator's setting, not product work
A fourth phase such as 'only when idle', or detecting whether the user is at the machine: slice 4

summary: Slice 2 of 'Checks cost less on a machine that is in use'. A project can say whether each check runs before review, at landing, or both. A project can turn on 'checks give way to the user' (off by default), which runs every check below the user's own work in priority. A check run that ends without judging the work is handled by what ended it: a merge conflict goes back to the builder, a Hub stop is re-run, a Hub fault or a check that ran out of time is retried once and then shown to the operator. None of these counts as the task's own failure. Each check's usual duration is shown beside its time limit. Product, general: nothing here is specific to AgentWeave's own repository.
